one_month_reasoning: The last close in the window is Fri 2026-10-30, since 11/01 is a Sunday. No Q3 date 8-K had been filed by 10/02 (EDGAR index, source 19), and DOCN's past Q3 prints came on Nov 2-7, so the Q3 report (guide $304-307M, $0.28-0.30 EPS) almost certainly falls after the window. The filings inside the window so far are routine: the Oct 2 Form 4s are a director's fee taken in stock at $127.17 and an officer's tax-withholding (code F) disposal at $135.01 (source 20). That is not a signal. The remaining risks are a pre-announcement tied to a capital-markets action (as on July 7), MUFG lease draws, hyperscaler capex prints in late October, and neocloud sentiment. With no scheduled company catalyst I use a near-symmetric lognormal with a median of about $139 (a tiny negative drift) and sigma ≈ 82% x sqrt(20/252) ≈ 22.5%.

fair_value.method: Value as of October 2027 on CY2028 as a proxy for NTM, using 125M diluted shares and ~$1.1B of horizon net debt (finance leases included, operating leases excluded). Weights: 40% P/E (40x x CY28E EPS $2.50 = $100), 40% EV/EBITDA (18x x CY28E GAAP-basis EBITDA $790M = $14.2B EV, less $1.1B = $105) and 20% DCF (11% WACC, 4% terminal growth = $85). The blend is about $100. If CY28 revenue reaches the thinly populated $2.69B MarketScreener consensus, fair value rises to about $110.

inputs_detail.derivation: CY28 revenue of $2.55B (+41%) sits between my round-1 +35% and MarketScreener's +48% ($2.69B) consensus, which is thinly populated. Capacity caps the upside: 155MW committed, about 60MW online mainly in 2027 and 20MW in late 2027/early 2028 (sources 6, 10). EPS grows a little slower than revenue because D&A is running +56% y/y in H1 2026 (source 1).

The infrastructure peer CY2027 street P/E median is 23.4x (n=7; range 14.5x-209x; one basis, see comps_summary). The premium is growth-adjusted and limited to contracted growth. A peer PEG of about 1.3 times DOCN's ~30% EPS growth beyond the horizon (CY29, decaying from +39% in CY28) gives about 39-40x, about 1.7x the median and inside the range. I cut it from 45x because 45x applied growth that is not yet contracted beyond the horizon.

bear.story: AI GPU capacity loosens or a nine-figure inference customer downsizes. 2027 growth lands at 35-40% instead of >50%, gross margin keeps falling (55% in Q2 vs 60%) as depreciation and lease interest build, and more lease or equity funding is needed. CY28E EPS comes in around $2.0 and the multiple settles near 30x.

base.story: 2027 growth beats 50% (about $1.8B), capacity comes online on schedule and CY28E EPS is about $2.5. The multiple compresses from 78x CY27 to about 51x CY28, so the stock ends slightly below today as delivery only partly offsets the de-rating.

bull.story: More nine-figure commitments, RPO above $2B, and CY28 revenue at or above the $2.69B MarketScreener consensus. CY28E EPS of about $3.0 at about 75x as the market keeps valuing DOCN as an AI-inference platform.

comps_summary.peer_range: One basis: calendar-2027 street (adjusted) consensus EPS from Finviz, with ORCL and MSFT calendarised and stockanalysis 'Forward PE' not used. P/E runs from 14.5x (ORCL) to 209x (NET), n=7; the loss-making neoclouds are not meaningful. EV/EBITDA is calendar 2027, computed as TTM GAAP EBITDA margin x CY2027 consensus revenue (my own constant-margin estimate, the same basis as DOCN's): 7.3x (CRWV) to 67.1x (IREN), n=8, with NET and FSLY not meaningful. Developer software (DDOG, MDB, SNOW, GTLB, TWLO; supervisor's 12-name median 43.2x) is a sensitivity check only, because those companies run 75-80% gross margins with no GPU capex.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DOCN today is ~78x CY2027 street EPS ($140.07/$1.80) and ~31x CY2027 EBITDA on my basis. I apply 40x P/E (1.7x the median, inside the range) and 18x EV/EBITDA (1.15x the median, inside the range) to CY2028 at the horizon.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium comes only from revenue growth that is contracted and structurally higher than peers': RPO is $894M (12x y/y) with a 3.7-year weighted life ($366M due within 12 months), 155MW is committed, and the >50% 2027 outlook was reaffirmed in the Q2 release. Because those contracts run past Oct-2027, the growth gap should persist through the horizon. I size the premium with growth-adjusted parity (peer PEG of about 1.3 times DOCN's ~30% EPS growth beyond the horizon), not with sell-side calls. I hold it below that level on EBITDA for three reasons: gross margin is falling, the growth is funded with leases and equity (two 2026 raises, MUFG facility), and returns on the GPU capacity are unproven.

thesis_break_reason: At $75 the stock trades at about 42x the ~$1.80 street CY2027 EPS, below the $77 March 2026 offering price, and only about 1.8x the 23.4x infrastructure median. That price is close to a no-premium-beyond-contracts valuation. Getting there would most likely mean the >50% 2027 outlook or the nine-figure commitments behind the $894M RPO had broken (churn, capacity delays, GPU price collapse), or that lease-funded capex forced a dilutive raise, rather than ordinary volatility. I moved it from $80 because my fair value fell to $100 and $80 is now within one ordinary drawdown of it.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my balance-sheet facts: net debt about $0.28B today (converts $465.5M after the 7/23 repurchase, no term loan, finance leases $578M) and 125M diluted shares. It corrected four things. D&A growth is 56%, not 65%. FY26 consensus EPS ($1.46) is above the $1.35-1.40 guide, so street CY27 growth is about +31%. Street CY27 EPS is ~$1.80, not $1.84. And MarketScreener's CY28 consensus ($2.69B revenue, which I re-checked) is above my +35%. I raised CY28 revenue to $2.55B and EPS to $2.50. I did not go all the way to consensus, because capacity (155MW, with 20MW arriving late 2027 to early 2028) caps 2028 and that consensus is thin. On multiples I rebuilt the comps on one Finviz CY27 street basis (infrastructure median 23.4x). I cut P/E from 45x to 40x, because a PEG-parity premium should use growth beyond the horizon (~30%), not CY28's peak. I cut EV/EBITDA from 22x to 18x, because only contracted growth justifies a premium and 22x was 40% above a 15.6x median. Fair value goes from $111 to about $100 (P/E $100, EV/EBITDA $105, DCF $85). I disagree with the supervisor's ~$112: it relies more heavily on EV/sales and on adjusted EBITDA that excludes SBC. Valuation predicts 12-month returns only weakly in a momentum, AI-narrative stock, so I do not centre the distribution on fair value. I blend a lognormal (median $124, sigma 0.66) 50/50 with a three-scenario mixture (bear $62/0.30, base $128/0.45, bull $225/0.25; scenario mean ≈ $132). That gives P(≥$140) ≈ 0.42 (round 1: 0.45) and thinner far-right tails (P(≥$350) 0.04). Research was limited to about 8 fetches: the EDGAR index (no Q3 date 8-K; routine Form 4s on 10/2), Finviz for DOCN, NET, ORCL, MSFT and CRWV, and MarketScreener. AKAM, FSLY, AMZN and GOOGL P/Es use the supervisor's Finviz spot-checks of my round-1 values. No option data was used.
